problem: parse coerces closed flags with bool() before delegating, so non-bool flags that raised ValueError on main are silently accepted and reinterpreted (e.g. 'False' becomes True).
validate_bounds is overridden as a no-op, so a closed unbounded end such as (None, 5, True, True) is accepted instead of raising ValueError as on main.
parse delegates to the private reference_impl._Algebra.parse as an unbound call on an unrelated class, coupling production behavior to a duplicated reference module.
bool() on unvalidated flags can raise non-ValueError exceptions from a hostile or array-like __bool__, breaking the ValueError contract.
The rework changes validation behavior but adds no tests for rejecting non-bool flags or closed unbounded ends.
is_number accepts NaN, so comparisons silently misbehave in is_empty and merge (already present on main).
